topic: How do HARQ retransmission limits balance throughput and latency in geostationary satellite links?
consensus_response: In geostationary satellite links, HARQ retransmission limits interact with various physical layer techniques to balance throughput and latency. Adaptive modulation techniques like AQAM are impacted by large RTTs, reducing their effectiveness in optimizing data transmission. Similarly, channel estimation techniques such as Least Squares (LS) or Maximum Likelihood (ML) are affected by high fixed latencies on satellite links. Furthermore, error correction codes like LDPC or Turbo Codes increase processing time and memory requirements due to large RTTs. To mitigate these effects, HARQ retransmission limits must be optimized to minimize latency while maintaining adequate throughput.
reference_context: Geostationary satellites operate at a height of approximately 36,000 km, resulting in high fixed latencies on satellite links, ranging from hundreds to thousands of milliseconds. This additional delay negatively impacts Quality of Service (QoS) and applications that are not tolerant against high latencies.
